Assignment 5 - K-means

Author

Hari Marasini

1 Goal of this assignment

The goal of this assignment is for you to explore the k-means algorithm learned in class.

In specific, you will be asked to:
- Use a different number of k than what we did in class,
- Validate the results of the new model, and
- Compare your results with those found in class

3 Questions

3.1 1. What number of k did you select? Why?

Code 
library(tidyverse)
library(ggcorrplot)
library(broom)
library(car)
library(factoextra)
library(ggpmisc)

weather <- read_csv("../data/weather_monthsum.csv")

#selecting numerical variables only for k-means
weather_n <- weather %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(year:strength_gtex))


# normalizing the data
weather_norm  <- weather_n %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~scale(.x)))
Code 
# Total error x k
fviz_nbclust(weather_norm,
             method = "wss",   #within sum of squares methods
             k.max = 10,
             FUNcluster = kmeans      #FUNction of clustering
             )

I chose k = 5. Because, the line graph plotted using “wss” method seems reasonably elbowed at 5th cluster.

3.2 2. How many observations are there in each cluster?

Code 
mod_km5 <- kmeans(weather_norm,
                  centers = 5,
                  nstart = 10
                  )
Code 
weather %>% 
  mutate(cluster = mod_km5$cluster) %>% 
  group_by(cluster) %>% 
  tally()
# A tibble: 5 × 2
  cluster     n
    <int> <int>
1       1   182
2       2    56
3       3   236
4       4   208
5       5    16

For clusters 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, there are 182, 56, 236, 208 and 16 observations.

3.3 3. Using the fviz_cluster() function, import here the original plot with k=4 did in class, and the new plot with the number of k you selected for this exercise. How do they visually compare? Which one seems to be a better choice, and why?

Original plot with k = 4

Code 
mod_km4 <- kmeans(weather_norm,
                  centers = 4,
                  nstart = 10
                  )


fviz_cluster(mod_km4,
             data = weather_norm
             )

New plot with k = 5

Code 
fviz_cluster(mod_km5,
             data = weather_norm
             )

Upon visual inspection, k = 5 seems to be better choice for me because the clusters have relatively less overlap and are more distinctly separated. In k = 4, two clusters (olive green and orange color) on bottom section of image, seem to be heavily overlapped without distinct clustering
